research_rationale:
EO 10033 (14 FR 561, signed 1949-02-08) regulates how the United States Government provides statistical information to intergovernmental organizations and, through the National Advisory Council, to the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank. I read the held Federal Register original in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10033.txt): number, title, date, signature and filing line (F.R. Doc. 49-1027) agree. The dossier inventory omitted Section 1, split the end of Section 2(b) into a separate fragment, merged Section 2(d) into Section 2(c) and ran Section 4 through a printed contents page, so I replaced it with 11 spans of the order's own text (Section 4 in two parts around the page break). The order has six sections with no expiry date or condition. Three later orders amended it, each held: EO 11269 (31 FR 2813, signed 1966-02-14, effective as of 1966-01-01) renamed the Council in Section 2(a); EO 12013 (42 FR 54931, signed 1977-10-07, effective 1977-10-09) replaced the Director of the Bureau of the Budget and the word Director with the Secretary of Commerce and Secretary in Sections 1, 2(a), 2(b), 2(c), 3, 4 and 5 and added a new Section 7; EO 12318 (46 FR 42833, signed 1981-08-21, effective 1981-08-23) restored the Director, now of the Office of Management and Budget, in the same sections and revoked the Section 7 that EO 12013 had added. The conflict flagged for this order (EO 12318 revoking Section 7 on 1981-08-21) concerns that added Section 7, which is not an original clause; the revocation ends no original clause, and the amendments are recorded as later events on the clauses they changed. The OFR disposition table lists exactly these three amending orders and no revocation. EO 12013 is cited through its American Presidency Project transcription (the Federal Register copy is held only as a custody record), so its amendment is cited by the transcribed sentence that EO 10033 is further amended and described from the Federal Register text and EO 12318's reversing provisions; this is a transcription-dependent citation under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Current predicate: original-plus-bounded-search route after reading the coverage of current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog. The order rests partly on section 8 of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act (22 U.S.C. 286f); no held source shows that section repealed, and the held eCFR text of 31 CFR 128.1 still cites it with the order. Every original clause is claimed operative on 2026-10-14.
